artifacts.summary: 8-phase plan absorbing the full paper-definition drift wave as one dated 2026-10-14 re-pin, with the in-tree verbatim judgment pass scoped to the re-pinned anchors; zero new Lean declarations.

memory_candidates.content: Absorbing a multi-anchor paper-definition drift wave in BimodalLogic has a fixed, reverse-engineerable procedure that is recorded only as narrative inside docs/reference/paper-definitions-of-record.md's own dated sections: bare `check-paper-definitions.sh` to get the drift list -> per-anchor `--resolve` to obtain text and sha256 (never transcribe; there is no --fix mode by design) -> replace the fenced latex block, the `sha256:` line, and the MANIFEST:BEGIN/END row for each anchor -> one dated `### Drift correction (DATE)` section inserted newest-first after the sentinel block -> re-pin PINNED_COMMIT/FILE_CHECKSUM/LINE_COUNT (a drift correction re-pins all three; a case-(b) coverage extension re-pins none) -> in-tree verbatim judgment pass -> `python3 scripts/export-lean-citations.py` -> gates. Two non-obvious facts determine the blast radius. First, 'verbatim' in this tree's docstrings means verbatim against the RECORD FILE, not against the paper (stated once, in passing, at FormalSystem/Semantics/FrameAxioms.lean:45-46), so the in-tree correction scope equals the re-pin scope exactly. Second, C35 in check-module-invariants.sh asserts scripts/lean-citation-manifest.json is byte-current by recorded span_start/span_end/keyword_line, so ANY docstring edit that shifts a declaration span turns it red; the record file's own narrative never mentions this step. Also: the paper is a live, separately-versioned external input that can move mid-task (observed moving between a research dispatch and the plan dispatch ~1h later), so every anchor count and hash must be re-derived at implementation time rather than carried from a report.
